Katja Makinen
Oulu, Finland
katja.makinen@mail.example
+358 00 000 0076

Profile

Signal processing engineer with 21 years at Hallaharju Space Systems in Oulu. Team-lead experience. Core expertise in embedded implementation, RF test, and estimation-algorithm design for ground-segment and instrument electronics.

Education

MSc Electrical Engineering — Oulujoki University, 2004
Master's thesis: adaptive weight computation for sidelobe suppression in linear antenna arrays.

Professional Experience

Signal Processing Engineer — Hallaharju Space Systems, Oulu, 2005–present

Long-tenure individual-contributor role spanning algorithm R&D, embedded firmware delivery, and RF measurement support for Hallaharju's radar and communications instrument products.

- Wrote production embedded firmware in C++ for Hallaharju's real-time signal-processing modules on a Xilinx Zynq SoC. Sample-rate loop at 200 MHz clock, interrupt-driven, full regression test coverage. This work required both the embedded systems discipline and a solid grounding in array signal processing from my electrical engineering background at Oulujoki University.
- Designed and executed the RF calibration campaign for Hallaharju's X-band ground receiver: element-level gain/phase measurements using an Agilent PNA-X network analyser in the company's anechoic chamber, followed by near-field antenna pattern verification. Responsible for the full calibration data pipeline from raw S-parameter acquisition through to the production calibration tables.
- Developed and maintained the extended Kalman filter used in Hallaharju's angle-of-arrival estimator for the ground-based direction-finding product. The filter fuses array-covariance snapshots with platform attitude data to track emitter bearing in real time. I wrote the original implementation, tuned the process-noise model against field-trial data, and supported it through three product revisions.
- Finnish citizen; have lived and worked in Oulu throughout my career.

Projects

Hallaharju X-Band Ground Receiver — Digital Beamforming Architecture (2012–2016)

Designed the digital beamforming architecture for Hallaharju's X-band ground receiver: a 32-element array with sum/difference beamforming and adaptive sidelobe cancellation. Responsible for algorithm specification, simulation in MATLAB, weight-computation optimisation, and hardware validation against measured antenna patterns. The beamformer module has been in production since 2016.

Hallaharju–Oulujoki University Collaborative Antenna Measurement Campaign (2018–2019)

Joint project between Hallaharju and the Oulujoki University's Centre for Radio Systems Research. Designed the measurement protocol, performed all data collection in CRSR's spherical near-field scanner facility, and wrote the analysis report. All deliverables — the measurement plan, raw data package, and 60-page final report — were produced in English as required by the EORA-funded programme under which the work was contracted.

Skills

- Adaptive beamforming (MVDR, LCMV, STAP variants)
- C/C++ embedded DSP (Xilinx Zynq, TI C66x)
- Python — production calibration pipeline at Hallaharju (instrument control, data processing, automated reporting; ~6,000 lines, maintained and tested, used by the RF test team)
- RF measurement and antenna characterisation
- Kalman filtering, state estimation
- MATLAB, Simulink
- VHDL (synthesis-level)

Languages

Finnish (native), English (professional working), Swedish (basic)

Other

Member, SESE Antennas and Propagation Society. Enjoy fell hiking and orienteering in northern Finland.
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Katja Makinen
Oulu
katja.makinen@mail.example

Kaikuvaara Oy
Oulu

Dear hiring team,

I would like to apply for the Senior Signal Processing Engineer position. I have spent my entire career at Hallaharju Space Systems here in Oulu, and I am looking for a new challenge within the same city and the same engineering community that I have been part of for twenty years.

Oulu's RF and photonics cluster is something I value highly. I have worked alongside Oulujoki University's CRSR group, attended and presented at local SESE section events, and watched the city's space-systems industry grow from a handful of companies to the cluster it is today. Kaikuvaara sits at the centre of that cluster — your SAR and scatterometer payload work is the kind of deep signal-processing engineering that drew me to this field in the first place, and I know from colleagues who have worked with you that the technical standard is high.

I also want to be straightforward about my motivation: after twenty-one years at one employer, I want a change of environment without leaving the domain or the city. Hallaharju has been a good place to work, and I have built up deep competence there — embedded DSP, RF calibration, Kalman filter design — but I have done the natural thing of becoming the person who knows where everything is, and I would rather spend the next phase of my career solving new problems than maintaining old solutions.

The specifics of my technical background are in the CV. I have built production firmware on real embedded platforms, designed and run RF calibration campaigns in anechoic chambers, maintained estimation algorithms through multiple product revisions, and written production Python tooling for the test team. What I want from this role is a place to apply that breadth to new instrument problems.

I would welcome the chance to talk in more detail.

Katja Makinen

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
